body.statement: For every fixed \(\kappa>0\), \(\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\varnothing\): ass:uniform-shell places positive mass below every positive propensity threshold, whereas ass:uniform-overlap-comparator imposes \(e(X)\ge\eta_-\) almost surely. For fixed \(n\) and \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), \(\lim_{\kappa\to\infty}\rho_n=(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\asymp n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\), uniformly under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\). The last display is the known bounded-overlap public-function benchmark of JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE. Thus the relation is a fast-tail rate reduction between distinct experiments, not a class inclusion.
body.justification: This known-comparator proposition records both the strict class separation and the exact surviving treated empty-shell term needed for a valid standard-case check.
body.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, establish the bounded-overlap product-rate benchmark; JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds, Section 6.1 and the conclusion, identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open direction. The new theorem concerns the separate dyadic-shell experiment rather than reproving that benchmark.
body.consumer: Readers can distinguish the genuinely weak-overlap class from the bounded-overlap comparator while checking that the four-channel formula has the correct fast-tail benchmark.
